description: CP-RISK-1 vectors (kernel 1.1.0). object-vectors: shape, disjointness and the RISK-1..6 conditionals - schema-enforced; `expected-rule` is the PORTABLE assertion (every implementation names the violated rule id), `expected-frag` is advisory (the field one schema library's diagnostic mentions). bundle-vectors: closure (RISK-7/8), typed Risk edges (RISK-12), the B.1.9 risk-coverage primitive (uncovered selections are REPORTED; --require-risk-basis fails them; only LIVE risks justify - retired or withdrawn ones are listed under `lapsed`; a predicate select makes the selection a lower bound), RISK-9/10 SHOULD-notes, RISK-11 treatment-out-of-scope (live risks only; undecided under a predicate select). risk-transitions: C.3c state machine - forward only, skipping allowed, retired terminal. Rules carry their why: each vector names the rule and the clause it answers to (ISO/IEC 27001:2022 6.1.2-6.1.3, BSI 200-3, NIST SP 800-30). The cases marked 'review finding R-n' were added when the proposal was landed in the repository (2026-11-10); each was demonstrated failing against the validator as first proposed.

object-vectors.rule: RISK-1 shape: scenario + owner-ref + state are the disjoint signature (ISO 27001 6.1.2 c: a risk has an owner from the moment it is identified)

object-vectors.rule: RISK-1: a risk without an owner is a worry, not a managed risk (ISO 27001 6.1.2 c 2). The object matches NO type - the owner is part of the disjoint signature - and the validator names RISK-1 rather than leaving the reader with 'matches no type'

bundle-vectors.name: retired-risk-justifies-nothing

scenario.en: Tenant keys exposed through a KMS export path.

bundle-vectors.rule: B.1.9 + C.3c: `retired` is terminal, so a retired Risk no longer justifies its control - req/1 is reported uncovered, with the lapsed Risk named. Counting it would make coverage monotone: a control justified once stays justified for ever (review finding R-2)

bundle-vectors.name: withdrawn-risk-justifies-nothing

scenario.en: Tenant keys exposed through a KMS export path.

bundle-vectors.rule: B.1.9: lifecycle `withdrawn` unpublishes the Risk object; an unpublished record justifies nothing (review finding R-2)

bundle-vectors.name: retired-risk-outside-the-soa-is-history

rationale.en: Risk R-2 retired with the legacy gateway; the control is no longer needed.

scenario.en: Tenant keys exposed through a KMS export path.
Tenant keys exposed through a KMS export path.

bundle-vectors.rule: RISK-11 binds LIVE risks: retiring a risk and then dropping its control from the SoA is the ordinary end of a treatment, not a contradiction. Without the liveness test this bundle fails for ever, or the retired record has to be falsified to pass (review finding R-3)

bundle-vectors.name: predicate-select-leaves-risk-11-undecided

scenario.en: Tenant keys exposed through a KMS export path.
Tenant keys exposed through a KMS export path.

bundle-vectors.rule: B.1.9 + B.2: a predicate select is engine-resolved, so the primitive's selection is a LOWER BOUND. req/3 is selected by the predicate; failing RISK-11 on it would be a false failure from incomplete knowledge. The primitive says 'undecided' and never guesses (review finding R-1)

bundle-vectors.name: deeply-nested-sets-are-expanded

scenario.en: Tenant keys exposed through a KMS export path.

bundle-vectors.rule: B.1.9 + D21: membership is a DAG of any depth; req/1 sits under eleven nested Sets and is selected. A depth cap would drop it from the selection without a word (review finding R-4)

bundle-vectors.name: everything-excluded-then-treated

rationale.en: Out of scope for this system.

scenario.en: Tenant keys exposed through a KMS export path.

bundle-vectors.rule: RISK-11 holds when the selection is EMPTY, not only when it is non-empty: the SoA excludes the one control the Risk leans on. Gating the rule on a non-empty selection lets exactly the fully-descoped case through (review finding R-4b)

bundle-vectors.name: treatment-names-a-set-not-a-requirement

scenario.en: Tenant keys exposed through a KMS export path.

bundle-vectors.rule: RISK-12: treatments[].requirement-ref names a Requirement. A Set id resolves in-bundle, so RISK-7 alone passes it and it resurfaces as a misleading RISK-11; coverage joins on Requirement ids, so the edge would justify nothing (review finding R-5)

bundle-vectors.name: component-ref-names-a-non-component

scenario.en: Tenant keys exposed through a KMS export path.

bundle-vectors.rule: RISK-12: component-refs name Components - the asset at risk is not a requirement (review finding R-5)

bundle-vectors.name: finding-risk-ref-is-landmark
bundle-vectors.rule: Finding.risk-refs is LANDMARK: the assessor's Finding and the organisation's register normally live in different bundles, so an unresolved risk-ref is not an error

bundle-vectors.name: finding-risk-ref-names-a-non-risk
bundle-vectors.rule: RISK-12: landmark does not mean untyped. Like a Mapping scope, the edge binds IF the target is present - a risk-ref that resolves in-bundle to a Requirement is a wrong statement (review finding R-5)

risk-transitions.reason: skipping is legal; RISK-2/3 make the skipped content mandatory
a risk identified and found not to apply retires without treatment
no backwards moves - a re-assessment that changes the picture is a new version of the Risk, not a state regression
retired is terminal; a recurring risk is a NEW Risk (the Finding `closed` rule, C.3)
